newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RED WINGS SWEEP DUCKS, RANGERS GO UP 3-1 ON DEVILS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RED WINGS SWEEP DUCKS, RANGERS GO UP 3-1 ON DEVILS.

text.p: Brendan Shanahan scored off a goalmouth scramble 17:03 into double overtime and the Detroit Red Wings completed a four-game sweep of their Western Conference semifinal series by outlasting the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim 3-2 Thursday.

In the night's other NHL game, Mike Richter made 35 saves to post his second shutout of the series as the New York Rangers took the heavily favoured New Jersey Devils to the brink of playoff elimination with a 3-0 home victory.

Shanahan got his first goal of the series on Detroit's 72nd shot of the game. Goaltender Mikhail Shtalenkov stopped a backhander by Martin Lapointe and Steve Yzerman's rebound attempt from just outside the crease before the puck squirted across to Shanahan. He was alone at the top of the crease and flipped it into an empty right side of the net.

The Red Wings posted three of their four wins in the series in overtime and advanced to the Western Conference finals for the third straight season. They will meet the winner of the series between Colorado and Edmonton.
Joe Sacco and Brian Bellows tallied for the Ducks, who were making their first-ever postseason appearance.

The Ducks grabbed a 2-1 lead on Bellows' power-play goal with 4:37 to go in the second period. He beat Mike Vernon with a shot from a bad angle at the bottom of the right faceoff circle for his second playoff goal.

Detroit tied it 9:09 into the third period on Nicklas Lidstrom's first postseason tally. Darren McCarty threw a pass while falling from behind the net and Lidstrom put a backhander from the slot through Shtalenkov's pads.

The Red Wings dominated after the second period, outshooting Anaheim in the third period and both overtimes by a combined 45-17. But Shtalenkov, playing for the injured Guy Hebert, kept the Ducks alive. His 69 saves were a franchise record -- regular season or playoffs.
He made an arm save on Kris Draper's blast from the left circle with 12:36 to go in the first overtime and used his stick to deny Draper again midway through the second OT period.
Anaheim went on the power play at 10:52 of the second overtime after Viacheslav Fetisov was penalised for high-sticking Warren Rychel. But the Red Wings held the Ducks without a shot.
Shtalenkov caught Igor Larionov's backhander in the midsection moments before Shanahan got the game-winner.
Sacco staked Anaheim to a 1-0 lead at the 3:01 mark of the first period, firing a slap shot from the top of the left circle past Vernon, who finished with 35 saves.

The Red Wings tied it with 1:35 to go in the period. Sergei Fedorov won a faceoff in the Ducks' zone and fed the puck to Doug Brown, who ripped a slap shot from the top of the left circle over Shtalenkov's right shoulder for his third goal of the series.
Anaheim had a chance to extend its 2-1 lead in the final minute of the second period, but Vernon dove to his left to stop Jari Kurri's breakaway attempt.

In New York, Adam Graves and Wayne Gretzky gave the Rangers a 2-0 lead after two periods and Esa Tikkanen added an empty-net goal in the final minute to give New York a three games to one lead in their best-of-seven Eastern Conference semifinal.
It was Richter's ninth career post-season shutout. He has stopped 132 of 136 Devils shots in the four games.
"Ricky's been spectacular the whole playoffs, each and every night. He's on a roll," said Gretzky, whose second-period goal was the 118th post-season tally of his brilliant career.
"Our team defence for nine games (including first-round matches against Florida) has been outstanding and when it has broken down, Richter's been there to make the big save."

But the win was a costly one for the Rangers. Talented young Swedish winger Niklas Sundstrom, who has five assists in nine playoff games, suffered a broken arm when New Jersey's John MacLean hit him with his stick as the Devils vented their frustration in the closing minutes.
No penalty was assessed on the play, but the Rangers were hoping to send tapes of the incident to NHL officials.
Sundstrom's injury and a brawl instigated by several Devils with 20 seconds remaining left Rangers coach Colin Campbell unable to enjoy the victory.
"It was a huge price to pay for the win tonight," said Campbell.
The Rangers can wrap up the series and advance with a win in New Jersey on Sunday.
